findings.title: Numeric coercion honors the documented D7 contract without raising
findings.description: `as_real` accepts any `numbers.Real` except `bool`, rejects NaN/infinity, and converts `Integral`-too-large-for-float into `None` by catching exactly `OverflowError` with an inline comment justifying the swallow (contract value, not an error path) — this resolves the archived task-review CONCERN that `bind_parameters` would escape with an uncaught `OverflowError` for `10**400`. `as_integer` mirrors it by delegating the float path to `as_real`, so both coercions agree on the same scalars except `Decimal`, which the design explicitly rejects for both, and which is pinned by `test_as_integer_returns_none`/`test_as_real_returns_none`.

findings.title: `InvalidParametersError` is now copy/pickle-safe
findings.description: Passing `issues` to `super().__init__` (not the formatted message) keeps `self.args` a tuple of `ParameterIssue`, so `copy.copy`, `copy.deepcopy` and pickle all rebuild via `__init__(issues)` instead of iterating a string. `ParameterIssue` is a frozen slotted dataclass and pickles cleanly, and `test_parameters_error_survives_copy_and_pickle` verifies all three round trips, fixing the archived code-review CONCERN that copy/pickle raised `AttributeError`.

findings.title: `OutputDeclaration.__value__` is an undocumented runtime protocol
findings.description: `_output_tuple` checks `isinstance(item, OutputDeclaration.__value__)`. For a PEP 604 alias this is the tuple of member types (`(SeriesOutput, LabelOutput, SignalOutput)`), so `isinstance` accepts any member — functionally correct, but `__value__` is a private `types.UnionType` attribute read at runtime, not an API the language guarantees. `test_declarations_reject` pins the behavior, so a future Python that changes `__value__` fails loudly rather than silently; a named module-level constant (`_OUTPUT_TYPES = (SeriesOutput, LabelOutput, SignalOutput)`) would read more clearly.

findings.title: Three "no element loops" guards have different scopes; the shared one is the weakest
findings.description: The loop-forbidding rule for this slice lives in three places: `test_import_boundary.py`'s `ELEMENT_LOOP_NODES` (includes `ast.GeneratorExp`), `test_confidence.py`'s copy (comprehensions, no `GeneratorExp`), and `test_labels.py`'s copy (comprehensions, no `GeneratorExp`). A generator expression over array elements would pass the two per-file guards but is caught only by the boundary-test guard, which no longer covers `confidence.py`/`labels.py`. The per-module guards also don't use the shared helper, duplicating node tuples and the walk logic. Narrow one of the three to array-element semantics or route all three through the shared `_loop_lines` helper with a documented node set.

findings.title: Unused `ParameterIssue` import in the test module
findings.description: `ParameterIssue` is imported but only appears as the type of a local (`issues[0]`) through `catch` — nothing in the file references the name, so `ruff` (`F` selected) would flag it as F401. The per-task check reportedly passed, so either the import is used in a part I cannot see or it should be dropped; worth confirming against the local ruff run.

findings.title: `bind_parameters` precedence: unknown keys named after declared parameters report `unknown_parameter`, and details are shared across issues
findings.description: Because unknown keys are reported as `repr(key)`, a non-`str` key whose `repr` collides with a declared name (e.g. `f"window"` with a `_StrSubclass("window")`-style str subclass, since `str` keys are excluded only when not exact...) — actually only a non-`str` key whose `repr` is `"'window'"`... concretely: `{"window"}`-like collisions require a non-str object repring to `"window"` is impossible, but `repr` of `str` subclasses is not used since they pass the `str` check. More realistically: a declared name that is itself the `repr` of another key (e.g. declared `window`, supplied key `'window'` as a `str` subclass is treated as declared — fine; declared `'window'`? not allowed by `NAME_PATTERN`). The residual case: a supplied key that is `str` and undeclared but whose name equals the `repr` of another supplied key — both become `unknown_parameter` with one shared issue name, losing one key. Edge of edges; the D8 wording ("a key that is not a `str` ... named by the key's `repr`") makes this behavior spec-conformant, so flagging it only as a documented quirk, not a defect. No action required beyond awareness.

findings.title: Design intent is consistently documented where behavior would otherwise look arbitrary
findings.description: The non-obvious choices are explained at the point of use: the exact-type `Timestamp.ns` check guards `np.fromiter(dtype=np.int64)` truncation with a comment; `_require_time_order` compares neighbours instead of subtracting to avoid int64 wrap; `LabelVocabulary`'s `pyright: ignore[reportUnnecessaryIsInstance]` marks a deliberate exact-set-or-frozenset check; and `Display`'s docstring states why the type is rejected by `canonicalize`. The D10 "no canonical type" rule is mechanically enforced by `test_labels_signals_declarations_define_no_canonical_type`.
